title: Legislative districts of Aurora

{{Short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Aurora''' are the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Aurora (province)|Aurora]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[Aurora's at-large congressional district|lone congressional district]]. == History == {{Further information|Legislative districts of Quezon}} The area now under the jurisdiction of Aurora was represented as part of at-large district of [[Quezon|Tayabas]] during the [[Malolos Congress]] (1898–1899) and [[National Assembly (Second Philippine Republic)|National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic]] (1942–1944) and the [[Quezon's 1st congressional district|first district of Tayabas]] from 1907 to 1941 and from 1945 to 1972. When seats for the [[Senate of the Philippines|upper house]] of the [[Philippine Legislature]] were elected from territory-based districts between 1916 and 1935, the undivided province of Tayabas formed part of the [[Philippines's 5th senatorial district|fifth senatorial district]] which elected two out of the 24-member senate. In the disruption caused by the [[Second World War]], [[Legislative districts of Quezon#1943—1944|two delegates]] represented the province of Tayabas in the [[National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic|National Assembly]] of the Japanese-sponsored [[Second Philippine Republic]]: one was the provincial governor (an [[ex officio member|''ex officio'' member]]), while the other was elected through a provincial assembly of [[KALIBAPI]] members during the [[Japanese occupation of the Philippines]]. Upon the restoration of the [[Philippine Commonwealth]] in 1945, Tayabas continued to comprise two representative districts, with the territory of the current province of Aurora forming part of the first district. In 1946, Tayabas was renamed [[Quezon]].{{Cite PH act|url=https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1946/ra_14_1946.html|chamber=RA|number=14|date=September 7, 1946|title=An Act to Change the Name of the Province of Tayabas to Quezon|access-date=May 1, 2023}}{{Cite web |date=September 7, 1946 |title=Republic Act No. 14 – An Act to Change the Name of the Province of Tayabas to Quezon |url=https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/9463 |access-date=February 21, 2022 |website=Supreme Court E-Library |publisher=Congress of the Philippines |archive-date=February 21, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220221145130/https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/9463 |url-status=live }} 5 years later, on June 14, 1951, Republic Act No. 648{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=648|url=http://laws.chanrobles.com/republicacts/7_republicacts.php?id=652|title=An Act Creating the Subprovince of Aurora, Which Shall Comprise the Municipalities of Baler, Casiguran, Dipaculao and Maria Aurora, Province of Quezon |date=4 June 1951}} established the sub-province of Aurora within the province of Quezon. Quezon (including the sub-province of Aurora) were represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region IV-A]] from 1978 to 1984. It was during this period that Aurora was proclaimed as a regular [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]], on August 13, 1979, by virtue of Batas Pambansa Blg. 7{{cite PH act|chamber=BP|number=7|title=An Act Separating the Sub-Province of Aurora from the Province of Quezon and Establishing it as an Independent Province|date=November 21, 1978|url=http://www.chanrobles.com/bataspambansa/bataspambansablg7.html}} enacted on November 21, 1978. Aurora's [[Aurora's at-large congressional district|first representative]] as a separate province was elected to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. The province was guaranteed its own [[Congressional districts of the Philippines|congressional district]] under the new Constitution{{Cite web|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|title = The 1987 Constitution of the Republic of the Philippines – Ordinance | Govph}} which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, and elected its member to the restored House of Representatives starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. In 2019, the districts used in appropriation of members is coextensive with the legislative districts of Aurora. Prior to 2019, when the province was just one congressional district, the Commission on Elections divided the province into two provincial board districts. == Senatorial representation == {{further|Philippines's 5th senatorial district}} Between 1916 and 1935, the territory of what is now Aurora (then part of the province of [[Quezon|Tayabas]]) was represented in the [[Senate of the Philippines]] through the [[Philippines's 5th senatorial district|5th senatorial district of the Philippine Islands]]. However, in 1935, all senatorial districts were abolished when a unicameral [[National Assembly of the Philippines|National Assembly]] was installed under a new constitution following the passage of the [[Tydings–McDuffie Act]], which established the [[Commonwealth of the Philippines]]. Since the [[1941 Philippine Senate election|1941 elections]], when the Senate was restored after a [[1940 Philippine constitutional plebiscites|constitutional plebiscite]], all twenty-four members of the upper house have been elected countrywide [[at-large]]. == Congressional representation == {{main|Aurora's at-large congressional district}} Aurora has been represented in the lower house of [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various Philippine national legislatures]] since 1984, through its [[Aurora's at-large congressional district|at-large congressional district]]. {| class="wikitable sortable" style="margin: 1em auto; font-size:100%; line-height:20px; text-align:center" |+Legislative Districts and Congressional Representatives of [[Aurora (province)|Aurora]] |- !District ! colspan="3" | Current Representative !Party !Population (2020) !Area |- ![[Aurora's at-large congressional district|Lone]] | style="background:{{party color|Laban ng Demokratikong Pilipino}};" | |[[File:Rep.
